one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Integrated manufacturer of power cables, conductors and EPC turnkey solutions for power distribution, with a strong presence in East India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: We are an integrated manufacturer of power cables, conductors and other specialised products for the power transmission and distribution industry. We also operate an EPC segment delivering turnkey solutions for rural and urban electrification, distribution, and power infrastructure development. Our key clients include Indian Railways, state DISCOMs, and private EPC players, both domestically and in select international markets.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Manufacturing - Power & Control Cables:** LV power cables, MV power cables, Aerial Bunched Cables (ABC), Control cables, Quad cables
- **Manufacturing - Speciality Products:** Aluminium rods, Aluminium alloy rods, PVC compounds, Speciality cables (custom engineered)
- **Manufacturing - Conductors:** ACSR, AAC, AAAC, AL-59, ACSS, Eco-conductors, MVCC
- **EPC:** HT & LT overhead lines, Substations (up to 33/11 kV), Distribution transformers and switchgear, Aerial bunched cabling, Underground cabling, Feeder segregation, Household electrification

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Strongly backward integrated: in-house production of key inputs including aluminium wire rods, aluminium alloy rods and XLPE/PVC compound, plus an in-house compounding facility for insulation, sheathing and semi-conductive materials used across power cables and conductors. Company manufactures its own wooden drums and packing materials and recycles/reprocesses scrap PVC/XLPE. Installed capacity for manufactured products increased by approximately 37.82% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026. Internal purchase of company-manufactured products used in EPC projects rose from Rs 2,596.41 million (Fiscal 2024) to Rs 3,052.71 million (Fiscal 2025) to Rs 3,543.86 million (Fiscal 2026). Forward integrated into EPC segment (entered 2015), providing cross-feeding of conductors and cables for its own EPC projects; apart from certain civil works, all EPC work is executed in-house with no third-party subcontracting.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body: Licensed stranding partner of TS Conductor Corp (USA) for advanced high-capacity conductors with carbon fibre composite core technology

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Increasing share of in-house manufactured products in EPC projects (from ₹2,596.41 million in FY24 to ₹3,543.86 million in FY26) improves margins and reduces supplier dependency.
- Order book growth provides revenue visibility; manufacturing order inflow increased from ₹13,542.70 million in FY24 to ₹21,232.05 million in FY26.
- Backward integration into aluminium rods and PVC compounds enhances operational efficiency and cost control.
- EPC segment benefits from synergies with manufacturing, enabling competitive bidding through cross-feeding capabilities.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand into higher-voltage transmission EPC works (66 kV and above), leveraging prequalification and bids placed for 18 projects worth ~₹9,000 million.
- Deepen backward integration to increase in-house sourcing for EPC projects, enhancing cost competitiveness and quality control.
- Grow international EPC footprint, building on the completed power distribution project in Togo.
- Leverage TS Conductor partnership to locally manufacture advanced conductors, reducing import dependency and capturing upgrade demand.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company has consistently invested in backward integration, increasing combined installed manufacturing capacity by approximately 37.82% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026 to 85,448 MT. It is prequalified and has placed bids for 18 transmission EPC works of 66 kV and above, aggregating to approximately ₹9,000.00 million, positioning it to expand into higher-voltage opportunities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the leading players by manufacturing capacity (85,448 MT) for power cables and conductors in East India.
- Strategically located manufacturing units near Kolkata and Haldia ports, close to raw material sources (aluminium, copper).
- Strong backward integration: in-house production of aluminium rods, alloy rods, and PVC compounds reduces third-party dependency.
- Established track record with marquee customers including Indian Railways (RDSO approved) and multiple state DISCOMs.
- Licensed partnership with TS Conductor Corp for advanced, energy-efficient transmission conductors.
- Robust EPC execution capabilities in difficult terrains (hilly, flood-prone, riverine islands) with over 43 completed projects.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- High customer concentration: Top 10 customers contributed 72.14% of Revenue from Operations in Fiscal 2026. — Loss of any major customer, particularly government/PSU clients, could significantly impact revenue and cash flows.
- Tender-based business model with government counterparties. — Revenue depends on winning competitive bids; contracts with government entities entail long credit periods, creating working capital strain and payment uncertainty.
- Geographic concentration in East India. — Operations and manufacturing are concentrated in West Bengal; execution in difficult terrains (forests, flood zones) increases cost and complexity.
- Working capital intensity. — EPC projects and government contracts typically have long gestation and payment cycles, potentially pressuring liquidity and requiring sustained borrowing.
- Raw material price volatility (aluminium, copper, PVC). — Primary inputs are commodities with fluctuating prices; inability to pass on cost increases could compress margins.
- Execution risk in new high-voltage EPC segment. — Expansion into 66 kV+ transmission EPC involves larger, more complex projects; delays or cost overruns could adversely affect financials.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Combined installed manufacturing capacity reached 85,448 MT as of March 31, 2026, after a 37.82% increase from Fiscal 2024.**
- **Total Order Book stood at ₹32,434.00 million as of March 31, 2026, comprising ₹16,688.92 million manufacturing and ₹15,745.08 million EPC.**
- **Expand into higher-voltage transmission EPC (66 kV and above) with bids placed for 18 projects aggregating ~₹9,000 million.**
- **Increase in-house sourcing of manufactured products for EPC projects to reduce third-party dependency and improve margins.**
- **Grow international EPC presence, building on the completed power distribution project in Togo and existing export customer base in Africa, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal.**
- **Leverage the TS Conductor Corp partnership to locally manufacture advanced high-capacity conductors, reducing import dependency and targeting transmission line upgrade demand.**
- **Utilize ₹4,900.00 million from the Fresh Issue Net Proceeds for pre-payment or repayment of certain outstanding borrowings.**
- **Cumulative EPC installations reached over 85,191 ckm of HT and LT distribution lines and more than 113 commissioned substations as of March 31, 2026.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand into higher-voltage transmission EPC works (66 kV and above), leveraging prequalification and bids placed for 18 projects worth ~₹9,000 million.
- Deepen backward integration to increase in-house sourcing for EPC projects, enhancing cost competitiveness and quality control.
- Grow international EPC footprint, building on the completed power distribution project in Togo.
- Leverage TS Conductor partnership to locally manufacture advanced conductors, reducing import dependency and capturing upgrade demand.
